question.prompt: Triangle \(ABC\) lies in the first quadrant. Points \(A,\) \(B,\) and \(C\) are reflected across the line \(y=x\) to points \(A',\) \(B',\) and \(C',\) respectively. Assume that none of the vertices of the triangle lie on the line \(y=x.\) Which of the following statements is not always true?

choices.content: Triangle \(A'B'C'\) lies in the first quadrant.
Triangles \(ABC\) and \(A'B'C'\) have the same area.
The slopes of lines \(AA'\) and \(CC'\) are the same.

Lines \(AB\) and \(A'B'\) are perpendicular to
each other.

solutions.title: Check reflection properties
solutions.explanation:
Reflection across \(y=x\) swaps coordinates: \((a,b)\) becomes \((b,a)\). Positive coordinates remain positive, so the reflected triangle stays in the first quadrant. Thus (A) always holds. Reflection also preserves shape and size, so it preserves area, establishing (B).

For a vertex \(A=(a,b)\), its image is \(A'=(b,a)\). Since \(A\) is not on \(y=x\), we have \(a\ne b\), and
\[
\text{slope of }AA'=\frac{a-b}{b-a}=-1.
\]
The same calculation applies to \(CC'\), so (C) and (D) always hold.

For (E), take \(A=(1,2)\), \(B=(2,3)\), and \(C=(1,3)\). These form a triangle satisfying all the conditions. The reflected points include \(A'=(2,1)\) and \(B'=(3,2)\), giving
\[
\text{slope of }AB=\frac{3-2}{2-1}=1,
\qquad
\text{slope of }A'B'=\frac{2-1}{3-2}=1.
\]
These two distinct lines are parallel, so they are not perpendicular. Therefore the statement that is not always true is \(\boxed{\text{(E)}}\).
